correctness.rationale: The claim specifies factors as distinct occurring words, not rotations with multiplicities. The parity splitting is exhaustive at length \(2m\): even windows are images of length-m factors; odd windows come from length-(m+1) underlying factors. Exclusion of length-three constant blocks makes the starts disjoint for \(m\ge2\). Circular equality-pair invariants distinguish even and boundary-defective odd classes and force singleton status of each new differing-endpoint odd window. The complete one-step extension recurrence \(E(2m)=\mu(E(m))\cup\operatorname{rot}_1(\mu(E(m)))\) and primitive-block lemma identify exactly the full T_k rotation orbit. The opposite-ended count \(D(2m+1)=2D(m+1)\) supplies exactly \(2m\) new singleton classes at dyadic doubling. Base length four is exhaustively enumerated, so induction proves precisely one size-N class, three size-2 classes, and \(2N-8\) singleton classes for \(k\ge2\). An independently scripted exhaustive factor-cover computation checked k=2..9 (N<=512), separately against a long direct prefix through N<=128; computations do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The known dyadic cyclic-complexity total \(2N-4\) is explicitly credited to Krawchuk–Rampersad Proposition 1 (2018), also stated by Shallit (2023), not claimed as new. Our theorem additionally identifies every occupied rotation class size, proves there are exactly four non-singleton classes, and specifies representatives of all exceptional classes. That information does not follow just from known aggregate cyclic complexity \(2N-4\) and ordinary factor complexity \(3N+6\): these yield only the number of classes and summed size excess, allowing multiple different distributions. The inspected primary papers discuss aggregate cyclic complexity, not this orbit-occupancy spectrum. The first 2014 paper also gives cyclic-language structural arguments, but the pertinent section does not state this dyadic distribution. Neutral semantic searches across published research records and literal/alias searches in literature did not reveal a matching theorem. This is best-knowledge originality, not a proof of absence.

value.rationale: Factor conjugacy is an established natural refinement of factor complexity, and its dyadic Thue–Morse aggregate count was already the object of a precise earlier theorem. The complete orbit-occupancy profile answers the stronger structural question of how this count is attained: precisely four classes contain any nontrivial conjugate pair, and one exceptional class contains all rotations of a complete morphism block. The explicit representatives reveal the exceptional configurations; the circular equal-pair invariant and extendibility recurrence explain the mechanism, not merely a numerical table. The fact is uniform at infinitely many lengths, exact, and not a relabeling of the known sum formula.
